products.name: InternLM (Shanghai AI Lab)
products.note: Chinese open-source LLM; academic research; cross-border data review advised

reading.body:
Shanghai AI Laboratory is a government-affiliated research institution in China operating InternLM, an open-source large language model positioned for academic research across Chinese universities and scientific applications.

The laboratory's stated focus spans model capability, embodied robotics, and AI safety frameworks, with recent emphasis on science-oriented systems that integrate language models, specialist agents, and physical automation. This portfolio suggests a research strategy prioritizing broad capability development rather than any single domain constraint. The 2026 announcement of AI-for-science results and a scientific discovery platform indicates the institution is testing large models as infrastructure for experimental workflows, from hypothesis through validation.

What matters for AI infrastructure is that Shanghai AI Laboratory operates within China's university and research ecosystem, not as a commercial infrastructure builder or power provider. The laboratory contributes to model capability and research methodology but does not control the compute, buildings, or power grids that determine how quickly those capabilities can scale. It represents the downstream user of infrastructure, not the constraint that binds it.

The data does not cover the laboratory's budget, its access to compute hardware, or the power requirements of its training and inference systems. Without those facts, the connection between its research ambitions and the infrastructure constraints that may or may not enable them remains unmeasured.

profile_text.body:
Shanghai AI Laboratory is recorded as a non-profit government lab. Its website describes recruiting global talent in artificial intelligence, large models, embodied intelligence, safe and trustworthy AI, AI for Science, foundational platforms, innovation chain, and management support. Since 2022, the laboratory says it has run joint doctoral training with Peking University, Tsinghua University, Fudan University, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Tongji University, University of Science and Technology of China, Zhejiang University, and other top universities. The site presents work on general artificial intelligence and scientific intelligence, including a 2026 WAIC science frontier forum where it released ten joint innovation achievements with universities, research institutions, and industry partners in life sciences, materials science, and deep space astronomy.

The site describes a scientific discovery platform called "书生·端砚" that connects scientific large models, professional agents, experimental data, and embodied automation equipment across the full research process from hypothesis to experimental verification. It also describes an open-source architecture called Mobius for long-range reasoning and scientific discovery, and an embodied intelligence full-stack engine called Intern-Robotics that addresses data, training, and application. The laboratory describes a general-specialized fusion technology system with three layers: a foundation model layer, a fusion collaboration layer, and an exploration evolution layer. It also describes an AI safety approach based on a 45-degree balance between safety and performance and a causal path through three stages it calls泛对齐, 可干预, and 能反思.

The laboratory's tracked AI product is InternLM, a Chinese open-source LLM associated with academic research. No litigation is recorded for the laboratory.
